page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.xlarge is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores running at 2.5 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, and it lacks dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers of compute and memory capabilities. In stress-ng and Geekbench tests, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor results, with large-block read-only bandwidth dropping to the bottom 10% tier. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as gzip compression and Passmark encryption tests, similarly register in the lower percentiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.ic5.xlarge offers a dedicated CPU allocation at a lower entry point, though it is constrained by its low memory-to-vCPU ratio and modest memory bandwidth. This makes it a specialized option where dedicated CPU execution is required but memory footprint is minimal. Tradeoffs include the complete absence of local storage and low memory capacity, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications.

Appropriate workloads for the ecs.ic5.xlarge are limited to lightweight, compute-bound tasks that do not require significant memory or high-speed storage. Suitable use cases include basic web serving, simple task queue workers, lightweight microservices, and low-traffic API endpoints. It is not recommended for database hosting, large-scale data processing, or memory-heavy applications.
